title: Repair TrailerModal rendering, fetching reliability, and dev diagnostics

requirements.summary: Fix TrailerModal visibility/stacking and ensure the YouTube iframe reliably renders and stops playback on close.
acceptanceCriteria: From both FeaturedRow and ContentGrid, clicking a media item’s trailer action opens a visible modal overlay above the page content.
When a trailer exists, the YouTube player becomes visible and playable within the modal (not audio-only, not hidden behind other layers).
Closing the modal stops playback and no audio continues in the background.
Re-opening the trailer for the same item after closing works reliably (no “stuck” blank state).

file_operations.description: Harden modal/iframe lifecycle: only render the iframe while the modal is open; force a clean iframe remount on close and on re-open; ensure the modal content stays above other stacking contexts by avoiding internal layering pitfalls and by aligning rendering conditions with Dialog open state.

Add a targeted global stacking fix for Radix portals (e.g., the Dialog portal container) so the TrailerModal overlay/content reliably appears above sticky headers and other high-z elements without editing shadcn UI source files.

requirements.summary: Make trailer fetching resilient: transient TMDB failures must show explicit error + retry, and modal re-opens must re-attempt fetch (no cached permanent 'no trailer' from failures).
acceptanceCriteria: If TMDB trailer lookup fails, TrailerModal shows an error message (in English) and a retry button.
Retry triggers a new trailer fetch attempt and updates the modal state accordingly (success/no-trailer/error).
A temporary TMDB failure does not get cached as “no trailer” for future opens of the same media item.

file_operations.description: Update the trailer React Query configuration so each modal open re-attempts the trailer lookup (even if a prior result is still fresh), while keeping true 'no-trailer' distinct from transient error states; ensure failures do not end up represented/cached as 'no-trailer' for subsequent opens.
Ensure the retry action triggers a fresh trailer fetch attempt and that re-opening the modal for the same media item also triggers a new fetch attempt (rather than showing a stale cached state).

requirements.summary: Add development-only diagnostics for modal lifecycle, trailer fetch outcomes, and iframe mount/unmount without leaking sensitive data or spamming production logs.
acceptanceCriteria: In development mode, console diagnostics clearly indicate: when the modal opens/closes, whether the trailer query ran, the resulting status (success/no-trailer/error type), and whether the iframe mounted.
In production builds, these diagnostics do not spam logs and do not expose API keys or user identity details.

file_operations.description: Align diagnostic helpers with the required categories (modal open/close/retry; trailer outcome success/no-trailer/errorType; iframe mount/unmount) and keep all logging gated to development-only execution without including sensitive values.

Ensure diagnostics are emitted exactly for: modal open/close, retry clicks, trailer result status transitions, and iframe mount/unmount; avoid logging any sensitive fields (e.g., API keys) and keep logs dev-only.
Gate any non-essential console logging so production builds are not noisy; keep trailer-related diagnostics routed through the existing development-only diagnostics utility.
